research_caveat: VERIFIER 2026-07-31: unlike the AWS pass, all six researcher source URLs on cloud.google.com WERE reachable this session (fetched raw via curl through the proxy after WebFetch truncated the long pages; every quote checked against the actual page text). Two hosts remain blocked by the network gateway (403 CONNECT): docs.cloud.google.com (both encryption whitepapers) — so the 'Not known' fields 3.1.2/3.1.3 could not be upgraded — and the session WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200), so the independent searches for those fields were done by directly probing candidate primary URLs on reachable Google hosts instead (trust-center/security fetched: no algorithm stated; DPA AES statement confirmed to be Google Distributed Cloud connected-specific, not general GCP).

1.4.2.locator: SOC 2 compliance page: 'Google Cloud regularly undergoes third-party audits for our products, systems, and infrastructure related to this standard. The SOC 2 reports are generated by an objective third party...'

Logged in review_queue.md; the page-level fact is verified, the Tavus-side evidence gate is not. | Corroborated by Google Cloud Platform SOC 2 Type II Winter 2026 (Mar 2025 - Feb 2026, EY), p.1: "SOC 2 Type II report on file with Tavus (Vanta)"

3.1.1.locator: GDPR resource center, encryption-in-transit passage: 'applied by default on Google Cloud to encrypt requests before transmission and to protect the raw data using the Transport Layer Security (TLS) protocol'
3.1.1.notes: VERIFIER CONFIRMED 2026-07-31: quote found verbatim on the fetched GDPR page. Independently re-checked for version numbers: zero matches for any 'TLS 1.x' string across the full fetched text of the GDPR page, the Cloud DPA, and the Service Terms — so the versioned dropdown options (TLS 1.2/1.3) genuinely cannot be selected from these sources, and 'Others - pls indicate below' (real standard: TLS, version unstated) is the correct conservative choice. The 'Encryption in transit' whitepaper that documents versions lives on docs.cloud.google.com, which is policy-blocked by this sandbox's gateway (403 CONNECT, re-confirmed this session). A human with normal network access should confirm the TLS version from https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/security/encryption-in-transit before submission and upgrade this cell to TLS 1.2 or 1.3 if stated. Free-text indication to accompany the dropdown: 'TLS (Transport Layer Security), applied by default; version not stated in Google's DPA/GDPR pages.' | Corroborated by Google Cloud Platform SOC 2 Type II Winter 2026 (Mar 2025 - Feb 2026, EY), p.53: "This service also offers transport encryption to enhance data confidentiality in transit. Google uses encryption to secure user data in transit between Google production facilities."

3.1.2.notes: Google Cloud Platform SOC 2 Type II Winter 2026 (Mar 2025 - Feb 2026, EY), p.116: "51. Customer data that is uploaded or created is encrypted at rest. CC6.1 ... Inspected the encryption configuration for storage devices with customer data at rest and determined that encryption was enabled. No deviations noted."

3.1.3.notes: VERIFIER: 'Not known' KEPT after independent check 2026-07-31. Same constraints as 3.1.2 (WebSearch budget exhausted; docs.cloud.google.com blocked). Direct check of the fetched GDPR page found only a Workspace-scoped statement ('Google Workspace customers' data is encrypted when it's on a disk, stored on backup media...') with no algorithm and no clear GCP scope; the Cloud DPA's 'backup' hits concern the Decommissioned Disk / Disk Erase Policy and backup power, not backup encryption standards. Per the field playbook, 'Not known' is common and correct for row 59. Ask Google in writing or confirm from the default-encryption whitepaper whether GCP backups are covered by the same at-rest encryption and with which algorithm.

3.1.4.locator: GDPR resource center, Encryption section: 'encrypt customer content stored at rest, without any action required from customers' (i.e. Google-managed default keys)
3.1.4.notes: VERIFIER CONFIRMED 2026-07-31: the 'without any action required from customers' passage found verbatim on the fetched GDPR page, and the customer-controlled alternatives (CMEK via Cloud KMS, FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated Cloud HSM, Cloud EKM) confirmed verbatim on the fetched Cloud Key Management page (https://cloud.google.com/security/products/security-key-management). OPEN GATE (unchanged): per the playbook the answer flips to 'Key generated by your company' if Tavus actually uses CMEK/BYOK for the in-scope workloads — human must confirm Tavus's key configuration before this cell is written. Logged in review_queue.md. | Corroborated by Google Cloud Platform SOC 2 Type II Winter 2026 (Mar 2025 - Feb 2026, EY), p.225: "Google uses a proprietary service to manage the distribution, generation and rotation of cryptographic keys. Files or data structures with user-generated content written by Cloud or App Engine services are encrypted with a key."

3.1.6.locator: Sensitive Data Protection product page: 'De-identification, masking, tokenization, and bucketing... De-identification enables you to transform your data to reduce data risk'; re-identification risk analysis including 'Computing k-anonymity for a dataset'
3.1.6.notes: VERIFIER CONFIRMED 2026-07-31: both quoted passages found verbatim on the fetched product page (de-identification/masking/tokenization/bucketing; k-anonymity and l-diversity computation). Researcher's caveat stands and is accurate: this is a customer-configurable Google Cloud service (Sensitive Data Protection / Cloud DLP), not something Google applies to Tavus data automatically as part of hosting.

3.1.7.locator: Sensitive Data Protection product page: 'De-identification techniques like tokenization (pseudonymization) let you preserve the utility of your data for joining or analytics, while reducing the risk of handling the data, by obfuscating the raw sensitive identifiers.'
3.1.7.notes: VERIFIER CONFIRMED 2026-07-31: quote found verbatim on the fetched product page — pseudonymization named explicitly as tokenization. Same customer-configured caveat as 3.1.6.
